entities.name: Siege of Nicaea
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Siege of Nicaea was a pivotal event in the capture of the Byzantine capital, Nicaea, by the Seljuk Turks in 1097. 

This pivotal event on June 19, 1097, marked the beginning of the end of the Byzantine Empire's control over Western Anatolia. 

The siege was led by the Seljuk general Kilij Arslan I and resulted in the capture of the city after a brief battle. 

The fall of Nicaea had a lasting impact on the region, paving the way for the Seljuk Empire's expansion into Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

The city's strategic location at the confluence of the rivers Sakarya and İznik made it a crucial stronghold for the Byzantine Empire. However, Kilij Arslan I's forces were able to breach the city's defenses, marking a significant turning point in the region's history.
